sentences.text: Datanglong was a large predatory theropod that grew to a length of roughly 8 to 9 meters.
The preserved length of the holotype specimen is about 0.7 meters.
The last dorsal vertebra features a pleurocoel, or pneumatic cavity, bounded by enlarged posterior ridges and the vertebral body.
The groove on the underside of the rear ilium blade, which attaches the musculus caudofemoralis brevis, is shallow with a short, ridge-shaped inner surface.
The last dorsal vertebra resembles Ceratosauria because its parapophysis extends beyond the diapophysis.
In 2014, the remains were described and named the type species Datanglong guangxiensis by Mo Jinyou, Zhou Fusheng, Li Guang Ning, and Cao Zhen Hunag Chenyun.
The species name refers to the Guangxi province.
Datanglong is classified as an extinct genus of tetanuran theropod with uncertain taxonomic placement.
Datanglong is classified within the unranked family Carcharodontosauria.
Datanglong belongs to the family Carcharodontosauridae.
The authors of the description placed Datanglong within Carcharodontosauria in a basal position, using a previous cladistic analysis by Matthew Carrano.

Cau noted that all synapomorphies Datanglong shares with Carcharodontosauria, such as pneumatic cavities in the ilion and the thin articulation between the ilion and ischium, are also shared with the Megaraptora group.
The parent group of Datanglong is Carcharodontosauria.
Datanglong is classified in the class Reptilia.
Datanglong lived during the Early Cretaceous (Barremian-Albian) in the Xinlong Formation of what is now Guangxi, China.
The holotype fossil, GMG 00001, was found in a layer of the Xinlong Formation, which dates to the Early Cretaceous, though its precise age is uncertain.
The time range for Datanglong is from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago, during the Aptian stage.
Andrea Cau suggested that the initial analysis focusing on basal Tetanurae might have misplaced basal coelurosaurians.
In 2017, Samathi and Chanthasit reported finding Datanglong nested within Megaraptora, sharing ilium pneumaticity with other megaraptorans.
In 2024, Samathi and colleagues recovered Datanglong within Coelurosauria and Megaraptora based on nine supporting characters.
Paleontologist Andrea Cau argued that the previous analysis was too focused on basal Tetanurae and incorporated few traits of Coelurosauria.
Cau included Datanglong characteristics in his own much more extensive analysis, which revealed that Datanglong would be a basal coelurosaurian.
